aborted.description: Always `true`: the group was closed and reversed.

AddClip.description:
Puts a clip on a track at a timeline position, overwriting what is there.

The clip arrives whole, with its own identifier, so replaying the command
from a log or a plugin reproduces the same project byte for byte.

start.description: Where the clip starts, in sequence time.

track.description: The track the clip lands on.

clip.description: The clip the effect is applied to.

plugin.description: Reverse-DNS id of the plugin declaring the effect.

index.description: Where in the target's marker list it goes. Appended when absent.

target.description: What the marker is anchored to.

index.description:
Where in [`Sequence::tracks`](sub_model::Sequence::tracks) it goes.
Appended when absent.

kind.description: Whether the lane carries picture or sound.

name.description: Display name for the track header, such as `V1`.

clip.description: The clip the crossfade fades into: the transition sits at its head.

duration.description: How long the blend should be, before clamping.

Analysis.description:
One analyzer run's findings about a media item.

`analyzer` is the identity of the analyzer that produced them, e.g.
`silence` or `scene-detect`. A media item holds at most one analysis per
analyzer: re-running one replaces what it found last time.

markers.description: Points and spans for a person to see, in media time.

metadata.description:
Scalar findings: loudness, a transcript, whatever the analyzer's own
vocabulary holds. Ordered by key so the project file stays stable.

ranges.description: Spans for a command to act on, in media time.

AnalysisRange.description:
A labelled span of a media item: silence, a scene, a spoken sentence.

Ranges are kept apart from markers because they are the input to editing —
a cut-silence command consumes ranges — whereas markers exist for a person
to look at. A range carries a [`MarkerId`] so that turning it into a marker
produces the same identifier every time the command is replayed; the host
assigns it once, when the analyzer's findings are stored.

id.description: The identity a marker made from this range takes.

label.description:
What the span is, e.g. `silence` or `scene`. Analyzers keep a small,
stable vocabulary: commands downstream match on it.

AppliedResult.description:
What one applied, undone or redone command did.

The project itself is deliberately not included: a caller that wants it
asks for [`PROJECT_GET`], so a chatty edit session does not serialise the
whole timeline on every call.

events.description: What changed, in the order it changed.

label.description: The label of the history step, as the undo menu shows it.

AudioStream.description: One audio stream reported by the probe.

label.description: The label the grouped step gets in the undo menu.

in_group.description: Always `true`: a group is now open.

Bin.description:
A folder in the media bin.

OTIO has no counterpart; the closest is `SerializableCollection`, which
carries no hierarchy. Bins nest, and hold media items by ID rather than by
value so an item appears in exactly one place in the model.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

media.description: Media items filed directly in this bin, in user order.

name.description: Display name. The root bin conventionally carries the project name.

BinId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a bin.

ChangeEvent.description:
One change to one entity, broadcast after the engine applied it.

The JSON shape is stable: it is what the Command API's event subscriptions
send.

command.description: The stable kind of the command responsible, such as `clip.trim_in`.

entity.description: The kind of entity that changed.

id.description:
The identifier of the entity, when the command names one. Commands that
mint an identifier — `track.add`, `sequence.create` — do not.

origin.description: Whether the command was applied, undone or redone.

revision.description:
The revision the project reached; every event of one engine operation
carries the same revision, and revisions only ever increase.

ChangeOrigin.description: Why the engine applied the command that produced the event.

oneOf.description: A command submitted by a client.
A history step being undone.
A history step being redone.
The entity now exists and did not before.
The entity no longer exists.
The entity still exists with different contents.

Clip.description:
A reference to a slice of a [`MediaItem`](crate::MediaItem) placed on a
track.

OTIO counterpart: `Clip`, whose `media_reference` is an
`ExternalReference` and whose `source_range` selects the used portion of it.
Placement on the track is positional, exactly as in OTIO: a clip starts
where the preceding items end.

The fixed set of per-clip parameters the MVP supports (docs/PLAN.md §5.1)
live on the clip itself: [`Clip::opacity`], [`Clip::transform`],
[`Clip::gain`] and the two fades. Their invariants are checked by
[`Clip::validate`].

effects.description:
Plugin effects applied to this clip, first applied first.

Each entry names the plugin that declares the shader and binds the
parameter values the user changed; the declaration itself comes from
the installed plugin at load time (see [`crate::effect`]). Empty by
default, and left out of the saved file when empty, so a project
written before effects existed still loads unchanged.

fade_in.description: How long the clip ramps up from nothing at its head. Zero by default.

fade_out.description: How long the clip ramps down to nothing at its tail. Zero by default.

gain.description: Clip audio level in decibels. Unity by default.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

name.description: Display name, shown on the timeline rectangle.

opacity.description: How opaque the picture is when composited. Fully opaque by default.

source_range.description: The portion of the source used, in source time.

transform.description:
Position, scale and rotation on the sequence canvas. Identity by
default.

ClipEffect.description:
One plugin effect applied to a clip.

Order in [`Clip::effects`](crate::Clip::effects) is the order the
compositor runs them in, first applied first.

A plugin targeting the `effect` world declares exactly one effect, so the
plugin id is the whole reference; [`params`](ClipEffect::params) holds only
the values that differ from the declared defaults, keyed by the parameter
ids the plugin declared. A value for a parameter the installed plugin no
longer declares is kept in the file and ignored when binding, so a project
that outlives an edit to a plugin still opens and still renders.

enabled.description:
Whether the effect runs. A disabled effect stays in the stack with its
values so it can be switched back on.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

params.description:
Values bound by parameter id; anything absent takes the plugin's
declared default.

plugin.description:
Reverse-DNS id of the plugin that declares the effect, e.g.
`com.subordinate.color`.

ClipId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a clip.

ColorPrimaries.description: The chromaticities of the red, green and blue primaries.

oneOf.description: BT.709 primaries.
BT.601 primaries.
BT.2020 primaries.
DCI-P3.
Not known, or not reported by the source.

ColorSpace.description:
The colour space a set of pixels is encoded in.

Per decision-3 the MVP stores these tags and renders assuming Rec.709; the
tags exist so adding colour management later is not a lossy migration.

oneOf.description: Rec. ITU-R BT.709, the MVP working space.
Rec. ITU-R BT.601 (standard definition).
Rec. ITU-R BT.2020.
Not known, or not reported by the source.

ColorTags.description:
The colour tags carried by a sequence or a media item (decision-3).

OTIO has no counterpart; this would live in `metadata` on an OTIO export.

committed.description: Whether the group held anything, and so became a history step.

ContentHash.description: A BLAKE3 content hash as 64 lowercase hex digits.

index.description: Where in the parent's children it goes. Appended when absent.

name.description: Display name, shown in the bin panel.

parent.description: The bin it goes inside. The root bin when absent.

index.description: Where in [`Project::sequences`] it goes. Appended when absent.

name.description: Display name, shown on the sequence tab.

settings.description: Canvas, timebase, audio rate and colour tags.

DeleteSequence.description:
Deletes a sequence and everything on it.

The inverse carries the whole sequence, so undo restores its tracks, clips,
markers and identifiers unchanged.

EffectId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a effect.

EffectValue.description:
A value bound to one declared effect parameter.

The cases mirror the WIT `param-value` variant one for one, with `Fixed6`
wherever WIT has an `f32`, so a value survives save, load and undo exactly
as it was set. `sub-plugin` converts between the two vocabularies.

oneOf.description: A continuous value, e.g. an exposure in stops.
A whole number, e.g. a sample count.
A flag.
A linear RGBA colour, one channel per element.
Index into the variants the plugin declared.

EntityKind.description:
The kind of entity a change touched, such as `clip` or `track`.

It is a string newtype rather than a closed enum because plugin command
kinds carry entity names this build does not know; the constants cover the
built-in model. Like an error code, an existing name is never given a new
meaning.

Filing.description: Where a media item sits in the bin tree.

index.description: Where in that bin's media list it sits.

Fixed6.description:
An exact number with six decimal places, stored as a count of micro-units.

This is the one numeric primitive for the non-time clip parameters. It is
`Ord` and `Hash`, so clips compare and hash exactly, and it saves as an
integer.

The serde form is the raw micro-unit count: an integer, never a float.

Gap.description:
Empty time on a track: black picture or silence.

OTIO counterpart: `Gap`, whose `source_range` carries the duration.

HistoryResult.description: The state of the undo and redo stacks, as [`HISTORY_GET`] returns it.

can_redo.description: Whether there is a step to redo.

can_undo.description: Whether there is a step to undo.

in_group.description: Whether a command group is open.

redo_label.description: The label of the step a redo would replay.

redo_len.description: The number of steps that can be redone.

undo_label.description: The label of the step an undo would reverse.

undo_len.description: The number of steps that can be undone.

bin.description: The bin it is filed in. The root bin when absent.

InsertBin.description:
Puts a whole bin subtree back at a given position.

This is the inverse of [`RemoveBin`], and therefore what redo runs after a
[`CreateBin`] is undone. It carries the entire subtree — identifiers, child
bins and the media filed in them — so undo is exact.

bin.description: The bin itself, exactly as it was.

index.description: Where in the parent's children it goes.

InsertClip.description:
Puts a clip on a track at a timeline position, pushing what follows later.

This is the rippling counterpart of [`AddClip`]: nothing on the track is
overwritten. Everything starting at or after `start` moves later by the
clip's duration, and a clip straddling `start` is split there first so the
half that follows the insert point rides the ripple with the rest. The head
of that split keeps the original identity, exactly as [`SplitClip`] does.

Only this track ripples. An insert that must keep several tracks in step
issues one command per track inside a history group, as the timeline does
for a drag.

start.description: Where the clip starts, in sequence time.

tail_id.description:
The identity given to the tail of a clip the insert point divides; a
fresh one when absent.

track.description: The track the clip lands on.

InsertClipEffect.description:
Puts an existing effect back into a clip's stack at a given index.

This is the inverse of [`RemoveClipEffect`], and therefore what redo runs
after an [`AddClipEffect`] is undone. It carries the whole effect —
identifier, enabled flag and bound values — so undo is exact.

effect.description: The effect itself, exactly as it was.

index.description: Where in the stack it goes.

InsertMedia.description:
Puts a whole media item back where it was.

This is the inverse of [`RemoveMedia`], and therefore what redo runs after
an [`ImportMedia`] is undone. Unlike [`ImportMedia`] it restores the item's
position in [`Project::media`] and in its bin, so the project file comes
back byte for byte.

filed.description:
The bin it was filed in, and where in that bin's list it sat. Absent
when the item was filed nowhere.

item.description: The item itself, exactly as it was.

InsertSequence.description:
Puts a whole sequence back at a given tab position.

This is the inverse of [`DeleteSequence`], and therefore what redo runs
after a [`CreateSequence`] is undone.

sequence.description: The sequence itself, exactly as it was.

InsertTrack.description:
Puts a whole track back at a given index.

This is the inverse of [`RemoveTrack`], and therefore what redo runs after
an [`AddTrack`] is undone. It carries the entire track — identifier, flags
and items — so undo is exact rather than approximate.

track.description: The track itself, exactly as it was.

methods.description: Every method this build serves, in lexicographic order.

Marker.description:
A named annotation over a span of time.

OTIO counterpart: `Marker`, with `marked_range` and `name`. A point marker
is a marker whose range is empty.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

marked_range.description:
The span the marker covers, in the time of whatever holds it: sequence
time for a sequence marker, source time for a clip marker.

name.description: Display name, shown on the ruler.

note.description: Free-form note, empty when the user has not written one.

MarkerId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a marker.

MarkerTarget.description:
What a marker is anchored to.

The JSON shape is a tagged union, so an envelope reads
`{ "on": "sequence", "sequence": … }` or
`{ "on": "clip", "sequence": …, "track": …, "clip": … }`.

oneOf.description: The sequence's own marker list, in sequence time.
A clip's marker list, in that clip's source time.

MarkersFromAnalysis.description:
Turns a stored analysis into markers on a clip.

The clip names the media, so the findings that apply are the ones stored on
the clip's own media item. Analysis times are media times and a clip's
markers are in that same source time, so the markers are copied across
unchanged: no rate conversion, no rounding, nothing to drift.

Two things are filtered out. Findings that fall outside the clip's
`source_range` are skipped, because the clip does not show that part of the
file; and a finding whose identifier is already on the clip is skipped, so
running the command twice is idempotent rather than a duplicate-marker
error. `label` narrows it further to ranges carrying one label — the way a
cut-silence workflow marks only the silence.

Identifiers come from the stored analysis, so replaying this command
reproduces the same project byte for byte.

clip.description: The clip the markers land on.

label.description:
When present, only ranges with this label are used and the analysis's
own markers are left out.

MediaId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a media.

MediaItem.description:
A source file the project references.

OTIO counterpart: `ExternalReference`, the media reference a `Clip` points
at. Subordinate hoists it out of the clip into a project-level list so many
clips share one entry, and so relinking a moved file is a single edit.

The stored path is always project-relative and the [`ContentHash`] identifies
the bytes, so a project folder copied to another machine relinks without
user intervention (docs/PLAN.md §5.6).

analyses.description:
What analyzer plugins found in this media, at most one entry per
analyzer (docs/PLAN.md §6.2). Empty until an analysis has run, and
absent from the project file while it is empty, so a file written
before analyses existed still loads.

color.description:
Colour tags read from the file, stored but not applied in the MVP
(decision-3).

hash.description:
Fingerprint of the file's bytes, when it has been hashed. `None` until
the file is first read, and on items restored from a project whose
media was offline at save time.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load, undo and relink.

info.description: What the probe found, when the file has been probed.

name.description: Display name, usually the file name.

offline.description:
True when the file was missing the last time it was looked for. Set by
[`MediaItem::refresh_offline`]; nothing else in the model reads the
filesystem.

path.description: Where the file lives, relative to the project folder.

kind.description:
`command` for an undoable mutation, `session` for a method acting on
the calling connection, `query` for everything else.

MoveBin.description:
Reparents a bin, carrying everything inside it.

The bin is lifted out of the parent it is in and inserted into `parent`, at
the end unless `index` names a position in the child list it lands in
*after* the lift. The inverse puts it back under the parent and at the
index it held, so a mis-drag in the bin panel is one undo.

# Errors

The root bin is the tree itself and has no parent, so moving it is refused
with `edit.root_bin`. Moving a bin into itself or into one of its own
descendants would detach the subtree from the tree, and is refused with
`edit.invalid_index`: the destination is not a position this bin can hold.
An unknown bin or parent is `edit.bin_not_found`.

index.description: Where in that parent's children it goes. Appended when absent.

MoveClip.description:
Moves a clip to another position, and optionally to another track.

The clip leaves a hole behind and overwrites what it lands on.

start.description: Where the clip starts afterwards, in sequence time.

to_track.description: The track the clip lands on; the same track when absent.

track.description: The track the clip is on now.

MoveClipEffect.description:
Moves an effect to another position in a clip's stack.

The index is the one the effect ends up at, counted in the stack *without*
the effect in it — the same counting [`super::ReorderTrack`] uses — so
moving the first of three effects to the end is `to_index` 2.

clip.description: The clip the effect is applied to.

to_index.description: The position it ends up at.

MoveMarker.description:
Moves a marker to another span, in the time of whatever holds it.

Dragging a point marker along the ruler is this command with an empty range
at the new instant.

target.description: What the marker is anchored to.

MoveToBin.description:
Files a media item in another bin.

The item is lifted out of the bin it is in and inserted into `bin`, at the
end unless `index` names a position in the list it lands in *after* the
lift. The inverse puts it back in the bin and at the index it held.

# Errors

An item filed nowhere — which only a hand-built project has, since
[`crate::commands::ImportMedia`] always files what it imports — is refused
with `edit.bin_not_found`, because there would be no bin for undo to
return it to.

bin.description: The bin it is filed in.

index.description: Where in that bin's media list it goes. Appended when absent.

NoParams.description: The parameters of every method that takes none.

Point2.description:
A point on the sequence canvas, in pixels, with sub-pixel precision.

The origin is the centre of the canvas: positive `x` moves right, positive
`y` moves down.

Project.description:
Everything a `.sub` file holds: media, bins and sequences (docs/PLAN.md
§5.6).

OTIO has no counterpart. An OTIO file is a single `Timeline`, so exporting
a project means exporting one [`Sequence`] at a time.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save and load.

media.description:
Every source the project references, in no particular order; the bin
tree, not this list, carries the user's arrangement.

name.description: Display name, shown in the window title.

root_bin.description: The root of the bin tree.

ProjectId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a project.

project.description: The whole project, in the shape the project file stores it.

revision.description: The revision the project was read at.

ProxyState.description:
Whether a reduced-resolution proxy exists for a media item (TASK-69,
TASK-70).

The proxy path is project-relative like every other media path; proxies live
in the `project.sub.d/` sidecar folder.

oneOf.description: No proxy has been asked for.
A proxy job has been queued or is running.
A proxy exists at this project-relative path.

Proxy generation failed; the message is for the user, the code was
reported when it happened.

Rational.description:
A strictly positive rational rate in units per second, held in lowest terms.

A rate of `numerator / denominator` means that one unit of a
[`RationalTime`](crate::RationalTime) at this rate lasts
`denominator / numerator` seconds. NTSC rates are represented exactly:
23.976 fps is `24000/1001`, never a float.

RationalTime.description:
An exact instant or duration: an integer `value` of units at a rational
`rate`.

The wall-clock length is `value * rate.denominator() / rate.numerator()`
seconds. All arithmetic here is integer arithmetic; no operation on this
type uses a float, so edits never drift (see docs/PLAN.md §5.1).

Equality and ordering compare the *duration in seconds*, not the raw
representation: `1` frame at 24 fps equals `2` frames at 48 fps. [`Hash`]
agrees with that equality.

The serde form is `{ "rate": { "numerator": …, "denominator": … },
"value": … }`: exactly the two integers, so a saved time reloads as the
same instant at the same rate rather than as a rounded one.

rate.description: The rate the units are counted at.

RelinkMedia.description:
Points a media item at another file.

The item keeps its identifier, so every clip cut from it survives the
relink. The command carries the new hash and offline flag as well as the
path, because relinking is what a successful search for a moved file
concludes with, and the inverse carries the three values the item had.

hash.description: The fingerprint of that file's bytes, when it has been hashed.

offline.description: Whether the file is still missing. False for a successful relink.

path.description: The file it now refers to, relative to the project folder.

RemoveBin.description:
Removes a bin and everything inside it.

A bin still holding media or child bins is refused with
`edit.bin_not_empty` unless `force` is set. A forced removal leaves the
media items in the project but files them nowhere, which is what
[`crate::commands::RemoveMedia`] then reports as an unfiled item.

force.description: Whether to remove it even though it is not empty.

RemoveClip.description:
Lifts a clip off its track, leaving the hole behind.

This is the non-rippling delete: the clips after it stay where they are.
Use [`RippleDelete`] to close the hole.

RemoveClipEffect.description: Takes an effect off a clip's stack.

clip.description: The clip the effect is applied to.

RemoveMarker.description:
Removes a marker from a sequence or a clip.

The inverse is an [`AddMarker`] carrying the removed marker and its index.

target.description: What the marker is anchored to.

RemoveMedia.description:
Removes a media item from the project and from its bin.

An item clips still reference is refused with `edit.media_in_use` unless
`force` is set: dropping the source out from under an edit must be
something the caller asked for, not something a mis-click does. A forced
removal is undoable like any other command.

force.description: Whether to remove it even though clips still use it.

RemoveMediaAnalysis.description: Removes one analyzer's findings from a media item.

RemoveTrack.description:
Removes a track from a sequence.

A track that still holds clips is refused with `edit.track_not_empty`
unless `force` is set: dropping an hour of cut material must be something
the caller asked for twice, not something a mis-click does. A forced
removal is undoable like any other command — the inverse carries the whole
track back.

force.description: Whether to remove the track even though it still holds clips.

RemoveTransition.description: Takes the crossfade off the cut before a clip.

clip.description: The clip the crossfade fades into.

RenameBin.description: Renames a bin, the root bin included.

target.description: What the marker is anchored to.

ReorderTrack.description:
Moves a track to another position in the stack.

The index is the one the track ends up at, counted in the list *without*
the track in it, which is what a drag in the track header does.

to_index.description: The position it ends up at.

ReplaceClipMarkers.description:
Replaces a clip's whole marker list.

The inverse of [`MarkersFromAnalysis`], and its own inverse: it carries the
markers whole, identifiers and notes included.

markers.description: The markers it is left holding, in order.

ReplaceMediaAnalyses.description:
Replaces a media item's whole analysis list.

This is the inverse of both storing commands, and its own inverse, so undo
and redo of an analysis are exact.

analyses.description: The list it is left holding, at most one entry per analyzer.

Resolution.description:
A pixel canvas size. Both dimensions are non-zero.

OTIO has no counterpart: it stores no rendering resolution.

RestoreTrackItems.description:
Replaces whole tracks' item lists: the exact inverse every clip command
returns.

An overwrite or a ripple can touch any number of clips, so undo restores the
affected tracks wholesale rather than trying to invert each side effect one
by one. It is a command like any other: applying it returns the same command
carrying the lists it replaced, which is what redo applies.

tracks.description: The tracks to restore, in any order.

RippleDelete.description:
Removes a clip and closes the hole, pulling the rest of the track back.

Only the clip's own track ripples; other tracks keep their timing, so an
edit that must ripple several tracks issues one command per track inside a
history group.

Scale2.description: A per-axis scale factor. Neither axis may be zero; a negative axis mirrors.

Sequence.description:
One editable timeline: an ordered stack of [`Track`]s plus its settings.

OTIO counterpart: `Timeline`, whose single `tracks` child is a `Stack` of
`Track`s. Subordinate flattens that stack into [`Sequence::tracks`] because
nested stacks are out of MVP scope. Video tracks composite top-down, so
later entries in `tracks` render over earlier ones.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

name.description: Display name, shown on the sequence tab.

settings.description: Canvas, timebase, audio rate and colour tags.

SequenceId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a sequence.

SequenceSettings.description:
The canvas, timebase, audio rate and colour tags of a [`Sequence`].

OTIO stores only the rate, implicitly, on each item's `RationalTime`.

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate in hertz; never zero.

SetClipEffectParam.description:
Binds one parameter of one applied effect, or puts it back to the plugin's
declared default.

A `value` of `None` unbinds the parameter, which is how a control is reset:
the project stores only what differs from the declaration, so an unbound
parameter takes whatever the installed plugin declares. The inverse names
the same parameter carrying whatever was bound before — `None` included —
so undoing a slider drag leaves the other parameters of the effect alone.

clip.description: The clip the effect is applied to.

effect.description: The effect whose parameter is bound.

param.description: The parameter id, as the plugin declared it.

value.description: The value to bind, or `None` to take the plugin's declared default.

fade_in.description: How long the clip ramps up from nothing at its head.

fade_out.description: How long the clip ramps down to nothing at its tail.

opacity.description: How opaque the picture is when composited.

transform.description: Position, scale and rotation on the sequence canvas.

analysis.description: The findings, carrying the analyzer they came from.

media.description: The media item the findings describe.

SetSequenceSettings.description:
Replaces a sequence's canvas, timebase, audio rate and colour tags.

[`SequenceSettings`] validates itself on the way in from JSON, so a command
carrying a zero sample rate or a zero canvas dimension is refused while it
is still an envelope, before it can touch the project.

SetTrackGain.description:
Sets a track's audio level.

The level is a [`GainDb`], so the command cannot carry a gain the model
would reject; it applies on top of each clip's own gain.

gain.description: The level the track ends up at, in decibels.

SetTrackLocked.description:
Locks or unlocks a track.

Clip commands refuse to touch a locked track — see
[`track_for_clip_edit`](super::track_for_clip_edit) — but this command
reaches it either way, or a locked track could never be unlocked.

track.description: The track to lock or unlock.

SetTrackMuted.description:
Mutes or unmutes a track.

A muted audio track contributes nothing to the mixer and a muted video
track nothing to the composite.

track.description: The track to mute or unmute.

SetTrackSolo.description:
Solos or unsolos a track.

While any track in a sequence is soloed the mixer silences every track
that is not, so solo is a lane property like mute: it is saved with the
project and undone like any other edit.

track.description: The track to solo or unsolo.

SplitClip.description:
Cuts a clip in two at a timeline instant.

The head keeps the clip's identity and the tail becomes a new clip butt
joined to it, so nothing on the track moves. `at` must fall strictly inside
the clip: splitting at either boundary, or outside the clip, returns
`edit.invalid_split` rather than silently doing nothing, because it almost
always means the caller aimed at the wrong clip or the wrong instant.

at.description: Where to cut, in sequence time.

tail_id.description: The identity to give the tail; a fresh one when absent.

StreamInfo.description:
What the probe found in a media file (docs/PLAN.md §5.2).

Filled in by the GStreamer discoverer in `sub-media` (TASK-13); the model
stores it so the bin, the timeline and an offline project can all show
duration and format without touching the file.

duration.description: Total duration of the file, exact at its own rate.

SubscriptionId.description:
The identifier [`EVENTS_SUBSCRIBE`] hands back.

It is unique within one connection, which is all a client needs: it can
only unsubscribe its own subscriptions.

TimeRange.description:
A half-open range `[start, start + duration)` with a non-negative duration.

Ranges are half-open so that adjacent clips neither overlap nor leave a gap:
a range ending at `t` and one starting at `t` are butt-joined. `start` and
`duration` may be expressed at different rates; comparisons are exact
regardless (see [`RationalTime`]).

Track.description:
One lane of a sequence: an ordered list of clips, gaps and transitions.

OTIO counterpart: `Track`, a `Composition` whose children are laid end to
end in order.

gain.description:
The lane's audio level in decibels, applied to every clip on it on top
of the clip's own [`Clip::gain`].

Unity by default, and defaulted on the way in so a project file
written before the field existed still loads.

id.description: Stable identity, preserved across save, load and undo.

kind.description: Whether this lane carries picture or sound.

muted.description:
Whether the lane is silenced: a muted audio track contributes nothing
to the mixer and a muted video track nothing to the composite.

Defaults to false, and is defaulted on the way in so a project file
written before the flag existed still loads.

name.description: Display name, shown in the track header ("V1", "Dialogue").

solo.description:
Whether the lane is soloed: while any track in the sequence is soloed,
the tracks that are not contribute nothing to the mixer.

Solo is a property of the lane rather than of the mixer so that it
survives save, load and undo like every other edit. Defaults to false,
and is defaulted on the way in so a project file written before the
flag existed still loads.

TrackId.description: The canonical lowercase hyphenated UUIDv7 of a track.

TrackItem.description:
One entry in a track's ordered child list.

OTIO counterpart: the `Composable` children of a `Track`.

oneOf.description: A piece of media.
Empty time.

A blend across the neighbouring cut. Unlike clips and gaps, a
transition consumes no track time of its own; it overlaps its
neighbours.

TrackItems.description: One track's items, as [`RestoreTrackItems`] carries them.

track.description: The track the items belong to.

TrackKind.description:
What a track carries.

OTIO counterpart: `Track.kind`, the `"Video"` / `"Audio"` string.

oneOf.description: Picture. Video tracks composite top-down.
Sound. Audio tracks sum in the mixer.

TransferFunction.description: The transfer function (gamma curve) pixel values are encoded with.

oneOf.description: BT.709 / BT.1886 display gamma.
sRGB.
SMPTE ST 2084 perceptual quantizer (HDR10).
Hybrid log-gamma.
Not known, or not reported by the source.

Transform.description:
The 2D placement of a clip on the sequence canvas.

The compositor applies scale, then rotation, then translation, all about
the clip centre (docs/PLAN.md §5.2). OTIO has no counterpart; this would
live in `metadata` on an OTIO export.

position.description: Offset of the clip centre from the canvas centre, in pixels.

rotation_degrees.description: Clockwise rotation about the clip centre, in degrees.

Transition.description:
A blend across the cut between the two items either side of it.

OTIO counterpart: `Transition`. `Crossfade` maps to
`transition_type: "SMPTE_Dissolve"`; the offsets are OTIO's `in_offset` and
`out_offset`, the amounts the transition reaches back into the outgoing
item and forward into the incoming one. Crossfade is the only transition in
the MVP (docs/PLAN.md §5.3).

oneOf.description: A linear dissolve centred on the cut.

in_offset.description: How far the transition reaches back into the outgoing item.

out_offset.description: How far it reaches forward into the incoming item.

TrimClipIn.description:
Moves a clip's in point, keeping its out point where it is.

A positive `delta` shortens the clip from the head and leaves a hole; a
negative one lengthens it, overwriting whatever lies before it.

delta.description: How far the in point moves later; negative moves it earlier.
How far the out point moves later; negative moves it earlier.

applied.description: What the undo or redo did, or `null` when the stack was empty.

VideoStream.description:
One video stream reported by the probe.

Frame rate and sample aspect are exact rationals; nothing here is a float.

color.description: Colour tags read from the container or bitstream (decision-3).

frame_rate.description:
Nominal frame rate. Variable-rate sources report their average here and
carry a PTS index instead (TASK-16).

sample_aspect.description: Pixel (sample) aspect ratio; `1/1` for square pixels.
